title: Ang 721–722: Tilang begins
hookLine: as the Word comes, Lalo, on ang 722
tomorrow: how long does water stay in a cracked clay pot?

lines: AND WHAT COMES IS AN ARMY.
cards: Some messages get softened before they're sent. A friend checks the wording, and the hard sentence becomes a gentler one. In Tilang, on ang 722, Guru Nanak refuses the edit.
He tells his friend Lalo: as the Master's word comes to me, so I speak it. And what comes is an army.
The hymn speaks of violence against ordinary people, so a gentle note for anyone listening with kids: it names harm without describing it.

teach.b: Tilang opens on ang 721 with Guru Nanak praying in Persian words: one plea I make to you; listen, Creator.
Then, on ang 722, the hymn to Lalo, whom tradition remembers as a carpenter the Guru chose to stay with.
In paraphrase: the invader has come from Kabul with a wedding party of sin, demanding a bride by force. Modesty and goodness have gone into hiding, and falsehood struts about.
The hymn names what the people suffered, plainly, and doesn't flatter the powerful. That's truth to power: the true thing about strength used badly, said in the words that came, unedited.
And since this is the week's last day, look at how it led here. Within, the fragrance in the flower. Plain prayers, Dhanna's lentils.
Quiet strength, a hand on the forehead. Strength, a beat that never drops. Tender, said once in the morning.
Each one honest. Tilang carries that honesty out into the street.

how: Sikhs often cite Guru Nanak's hymn to Lalo on ang 722 when speaking about naming injustice, and tell the story of the Guru staying with Bhai Lalo, a carpenter.

games.q: in a meeting, your manager presents a teammate's project as his own. you saw who did it. what fits ang 722?
o: tell the teammate privately later, and leave it there.
say plainly, without insult, whose work it was.
say nothing; correcting a boss isn't your place.
games.why: Guru Nanak speaks as the Word comes and names what power did, without flattering it. truth to power can be calm, and still be said.

practice: Take a pen and write one true sentence you've been softening, for your eyes only, and don't edit it. Then set the pen down, rest your hands, and sit with the sentence as it is.

carryVoice: Truth to power: speak as the word comes, without the edit. A week, done; fifteen thirty-three.
